title: Latchkey ops notebook - overnight quickref
notes:
TL;DR: quiet start, DB replica lag flared at 03:12 (see INFR-8421), applied short-window throttle on traffic-routing to replicas; primary healthy. Leaving sticky notes for next shift and a few TODOs.

SHIFT SUMMARY:
- Took over at 22:00 PT. Night baseline: low traffic, scheduled batch jobs start ~01:00.
- 03:12 - Pager: replica-lag-alert (avg lag ~ 9s across zone-us-west-2b). Triggered autoswitch heuristic, some writes were queued.
- 03:18 - manually scaled read-traffic down to primary for affected customer routes (temp route rule: route-read: prefer-primary=1.0).
- 03:22 - restarted replica node rdb-03 after IO wait spike; lag returned below threshold by 03:34.
- No other high-severity incidents. Minor error spikes in hosted-api /v1/embeddings (rate-limiter warnings) between 00:45-01:10, self-resolved after rate-limit bump.

ONGOING WORK / CONTEXT:
- INFR-8421: replica lag root-cause investigation in progress. Suspect: heavy background compaction + burst of ingest from a single customer (acct: acme-analytics). Priya is pairing with DB infra team on compaction schedule change (see linked PR).
- Temporary routing change (tag: route-read-temp-2024-11-07) applied at 03:18; remember to roll back if the replication stabilizes permanently.
- Perf test scheduled 11/09 02:00 PT that will run synthetic traffic (low risk but will exercise cache layers).

TEMPORARY MITIGATIONS APPLIED (notes to next shift):
- Read routing set to prefer primary for routes: /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank (applied via traffic-policy v2 console).
- Replica restart performed on rdb-03 (node-id: rdb-03). Node shows healthy metrics now: cpu<30%, iowait dropped.
- Short-term firewall rule: blocked a suspicious client IP that was making very high concurrent snapshot requests (IP: 18.135.44.21) — recorded in incident notes.

RUNBOOK SNIPPETS (for quick execs) :
- Check replica lag (CLI): 
  redwood-dbctl replica status --region us-west-2 --format brief
- Force sync check: 
  redwood-dbctl replica check-sync rdb-03 --verbose
- Scale traffic to primary (temporary): 
  rw-trafficctl set-policy route-read-temp-2024-11-07 --prefer-primary 1.0 --apply
- Revert traffic policy: 
  rw-trafficctl delete-policy route-read-temp-2024-11-07 || rw-trafficctl set-policy route-default --apply

ESCALATION (if lag persists > 30s for > 10m):
- Page DB infra lead (PagerDuty): Priya Raman (oncall). If no response in 10m, page Eng SRE manager Ethan Brooks.
- If replicas fail health probes: spin up warm replacement rdb-05 (runbook: infra/db/warm-node.md).

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm if compaction window needs permanent adjustment or if the offending customer ingestion pattern can be mitigated via quota. Action: Priya to file quota request for acct acme-analytics (JIRA: INFR-8423).
- [ ] Follow up on snapshot throttling thresholds — current default may be too permissive during low traffic and causes IO spikes.
- [ ] Add a synthetic monitor that kicks off small writes to replicas every 10m to catch lag earlier. (Proposal draft in GH PR 318).

HANDOFF CHECKLIST (what I will leave as-is unless changed):
- Incident notes added to INFR-8421 (timeline + commands executed).
- Traffic policy tag: route-read-temp-2024-11-07 (do not delete without confirming replication stable for 2h).
- rdb-03 node status: healthy; last restart: 2024-11-07T03:22:00Z.
- Open retention: keep monitoring replica lag for next 4 hours, escalate if >30s.

QUICK COMMANDS (copy-paste ready):
- replica status: redwood-dbctl replica status --region us-west-2 --format brief
- restart node: redwood-infractl node restart rdb-03 --reason "overnight lag recovery"
- set temp routing: rw-trafficctl set-policy route-read-temp-2024-11-07 --prefer-primary 1.0 --apply

NOTES TO SELF (scratchy):
- if acme bursts again, try temporary ingest throttle via rate-limit policy pre-bucket rather than full account quota (less customer-visible).
- ping product to ask if they can delay heavy sync job scheduled at 02:00 for non-critical tenants.

RANDOM OBSERVATIONS / IDEAS:
- might be worth a small healthcheck lambda that inspects replica lag and auto-scales read weight down for 2m buckets; simpler than full autoswitch.
- create a short 3-step micro-runbook for DB restarts (so juniors can act quickly) — pair with Priya on weekday to capture safety checks.

ATTACHMENTS / LINKS I used during shift:
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C013INFRA/p170... (refer to pinned messages in #infra-oncall)
- Incident: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFR-8421
- PR for compaction window tweaks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-infra/pull/318

SIGN-OFF:
- Leaving system in a stable state but with temporary routing in place. Next oncall: please monitor replica lag and undo routing change only when stable for 2+ hours and no recurring ingestion spikes.

-- Jordan
